item.title: Tailoring resonator geometry for astigmatism compensation with structured light in birefringent optical cavities
item.description: arXiv:2611.08575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we experimentally investigate the astigmatism induced by a birefringent crystal inside an optical cavity and demonstrate a geometric compensation strategy for structured modes carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM). We show that the astigmatism observed in the semimonolithic configuration can be fully compensated by introducing a third mirror to fold the cavity, thereby exploiting the geometric astigmatism arising from oblique incidence on the curved mirror. By performing a study of the resonator geometry, both theoretical and experimental results confirm that this approach enables the preservation of OAM between the pump beam and the converted signal and idler modes, providing an effective design strategy for birefringent optical cavities.
item.dc:creator: J. C. de Carvalho Jr., R. F. Barros, A. Z. Khoury, C. E. R. Souza, G. B. Alves

item.title: Modulation Induced Memory Resonances in Dynamically Driven Optical Cavities
item.description: arXiv:2611.08622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal modulation of optical cavities provides a powerful mechanism for controlling photonic states beyond the static cavity paradigm. Here, we investigate the dynamics of periodically driven optical cavities using a time-dependent cavity-field model with modulated resonance frequencies. We demonstrate modulation-induced tuning of cavity resonances and analyze the resulting intracavity field evolution in both amplitude and phase. The interplay between periodic modulation and cavity dissipation gives rise to pronounced hysteretic behavior, revealing memory effects associated with the finite photon lifetime of the cavity. By quantifying the hysteresis area as a function of modulation frequency, we identify distinct memory resonances characterized by enhanced field-history dependence at specific driving frequencies. Furthermore, we examine the time-resolved local density of optical states (LDOS) and show that temporal modulation enables dynamic spectral redistribution of photonic states, with the degree of confinement governed by the cavity loss rate. Our results establish a simple framework for understanding and engineering memory effects in dynamically driven optical resonators and provide new opportunities for tunable photonic environments, dynamic LDOS control, and reconfigurable light-matter interactions.
item.dc:creator: Faizan H. Lone

item.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.08733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40 $\mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$, this low-loss HfO$_{2}$ metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free DUV biosensing.
item.dc:creator: Be\'ata Idesov\'a, Alexander A. Antonov, Lina Rohrer, Leonardo de Souza Menezes, Andreas Tittl, Tom\'a\v{s} \v{S}ikola, Filip Ligmajer

item.title: Laser-Direct-Written polymer WGM microring laser integrated on a fiber tip for refractive index sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.08805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) microlasers are promising for refractometric sensing, but their practical implementation can be limited by the need for stable resonator-coupler alignment. Here, we demonstrate a Rhodamine B-doped polymer WGM microring laser directly fabricated on an optical-fiber tip, eliminating the external resonator-fiber coupling interface at the sensing head. Micro-droplet coating and UV laser direct writing are combined for fabrication, while finite-difference time-domain simulations guide the microring laser design. The microlasers operate in air and water with thresholds of 0.224 uJ and 0.458 uJ, respectively. Refractometric measurements in aqueous glucose solutions yield a bulk refractive index sensitivity of 364.95 nm/RIU and a detection limit of 2.47 x 10^(-4) RIU. Water-induced polymer changes and photobleaching are also investigated. This fiber-tip architecture provides a basis for probe-based refractometric sensing in environmental and biochemical applications.
item.dc:creator: Mobin Yaghoobi, Seyedeh Mahshad Hosseini, Leila Hajshahvaladi, Gholam-Mohammad Parsanasab, Mohammad Ismail Zibaii

item.title: Differential chiral sensing at exceptional points in intrinsically chiral metastructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.08822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discriminating opposite enantiomers through their weak chiroptical responses remains a fundamental challenge in optical sensing. Exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian singularities at which eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, offer a route to enhanced spectral responses through their characteristic square-root eigenvalue splitting. However, their potential for chiral discrimination remains largely unexplored. We demonstrate exceptional points in an intrinsically chiral hybrid metamaterial and reveal strongly asymmetric responses to enantiomeric perturbations. The interplay between intrinsic chirality and non-Hermitian degeneracy is realized through the coupling of a chiral plasmonic nanoantenna array to a photonic crystal slab. We observe characteristic complex-square-root scaling, with both resonance frequencies and loss-rates exhibiting pronounced handedness dependence. Remarkably, opposite enantiomers produce complex mode splittings that differ by more than an order of magnitude. Our findings establish intrinsic chirality as a new degree of freedom in non-Hermitian physics and reveal a fundamental route toward topological singularities enhanced discrimination of chiral matter.
item.dc:creator: Suzit Hasan Nayem, Zhanni Wu, Mariusz Drong, Kamyar Behrouzi, Boubacar Kant\'e

item.title: Self-injection-locked dark-soliton Kerr optical frequency combs with high even-order normal dispersion
item.description: arXiv:2611.08848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We numerically investigate dissipative dark-soliton (DDS) microcombs under the action of pure high even-order normal (HEON) dispersion in a microresonator with the self-injection locking (SIL). Pure 4th, 6th, 10th, and 14th-order normal dispersion can support DDSs formed by interlocked switching waves, directly excited through a SIL-based turnkey scheme without detuning sweeps. Compared to the pure 4th-order case, the switching-wave tail oscillation period increases and its decay rate decreases with the increase of the dispersion order. Although the overall comb bandwidth narrows, the number of non-pump comb lines above a common absolute power threshold increases. Furthermore, the feedback phase controls the DDS duty cycle and intracavity comb-line power distribution, while the increase of the pump power improves the estimated pump-to-comb output conversion efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Lei Shi, Rujiang Li, Shilong Liu, Dumitru Mihalache, Boris A. Malomed, Pengfei Li

item.title: Optical microscopy for pathological imaging: past, present, and future
item.description: arXiv:2611.09104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Histopathology, the microscopic examination of stained tissue sections, remains the gold standard for pathology imaging, but its bright-field imaging is largely morphological. Advanced optical microscopy techniques move beyond this by exploiting diverse light-matter interactions, and are increasingly applied to pathological imaging. By capturing signals such as refractive index, polarisation, harmonic generation, Brillouin shift, and molecular vibrations, these microscopy techniques can provide quantitative or semi-quantitative information on tissue structure, mechanics, and chemical or molecular composition. In this review, we summarise the physical principles, key quantitative parameters, and representative pathological applications of seven modalities--optical diffraction tomography, polarisation microscopy, second-harmonic generation microscopy, third-harmonic generation microscopy, Brillouin microscopy, Raman microscopy, and fluorescence microscopy. We also discuss progress in artificial intelligence that supports reconstruction, analysis, and interpretation across these modalities, together with emerging trends in multimodal integration. Overall, this review shows how different optical contrasts can complement routine histopathology, while outlining the challenges and opportunities that will shape their clinical translation.
item.dc:creator: Runchen Zhang, Xiaoyi Shang, Liangyu Deng, Jingyu Wang, Xiaoyu Zheng, Lanyu Cui, Yao Du, Jiaxin Zhuang, Yifei Ma, Wanying Liu, Limei Guo, Lin Luo, Zhiyi Liu, Stephen M. Morris, Honghui He, Chao He

item.title: Raytracing and quantifying the inferior mirage
item.description: arXiv:2611.09131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using custom raytracing code, we explore several features of the inferior mirage that are not widely discussed, such as the blurring in the mirage image, and what happens to the light in the direct image region that is replaced by the mirage image. The raytracing model also clarifies how to quantify the mirage, and we provide expressions to calculate the angular extent of the mirage under given thermal conditions and measurement geometry.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Hagen, Lucas Reyes Bentancor, Kakeru Tanaka, Norimasa Hanaya, Momo Shoda, Hiroki Maki, Takuma Ando, Keisaku Yoshizawa, Kayo Suzuki, Yume Yamada, Asana Kumakura

item.title: An acousto-optic colorimeter for color psychophysics
item.description: arXiv:2611.09144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A complete model of human color perception requires the ability to present any color as a stimulus.Most existing measurements were collected with physical color samples, and current laboratory generators, such as displays and multi-primary LED systems, work with a small number of fixed primaries. Published color-difference data therefore cover about 40\% of the CIE~$xy$ chromaticity diagram, while commercial wide-gamut displays already reach two thirds of it and need difference metrics there. We describe an acousto-optic colorimeter that lets the experimenter choose the primaries. The device selects up to four narrow bands from a supercontinuum (white-light) laser, each with electronically set wavelength and intensity, and covers 95\% of the CIE~$xy$ chromaticity diagram. Threshold-scale color differences, presented in alternation as in a discrimination experiment, are reproduced with a mean error of 0.08--0.12 CIEDE2000 units ($\Delta E_{00}$) at five CIE-recommended color centers. Because one color can be built from many combinations of narrow bands, the bands are chosen for the task: the finest adjustment for color matching, the least disagreement between observers for color-difference measurement. In simulations with 151~individual observers from a published dataset, with these bands observers see colors 0.6--1.9~$\Delta E_{00}$ from the intended one on average, against 1.2--2.5~$\Delta E_{00}$ on a calibrated wide-gamut LCD, lower at every center. The approach applies to any narrowband source and lets experimenters use saturated colors while limiting the effect of individual differences in color vision.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Korchagin, Georgiy Lobarev, Pavel Aksentsev, Pavel Maximov, Maria Gracheva, Olga Polschikova, Egor Ershov

item.title: Low-Rank Iteration for Efficient Calculations of Topological Surface States
item.description: arXiv:2611.09165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface states are hallmarks of topological phases, and their efficient computation is crucial for topology characterization. Conventional supercell methods (SCM) approximate semi-infinite systems as finite periodic ones, but suffer from high computational cost, artificial inter-surface coupling, and slow convergence near band edges. Recently, boundary problems for semi-infinite systems have been recast as block-tridiagonal equations and solved by the cyclic reduction method (CRM) and the transfer matrix method (TMM). However, these approaches remain resource-intensive, as fine-mesh discretization produces very large matrices. Recognizing the intrinsic sparsity and low rank of these matrices, we develop a low-rank iterative method (LIM) with stochastic trace estimation that substantially reduces complexity and memory without sacrificing accuracy, while remaining straightforwardly parallelizable. Benchmarks on 2D and 3D topological systems show orders-of-magnitude acceleration over CRM and TMM. LIM extends readily to heterostructures, defective interfaces, and non-Hermitian systems, providing an efficient platform for topological and plasmonic surface phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Kaiqi Liu, Changsheng He, Zihan Xie, Shulin Sun, Lei Zhou, Shaojie Ma

item.title: When is an Optical Design Problem a Mass Transfer Problem?
item.description: arXiv:2611.09219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates whether optical design problems can be represented as Monge--Kantorovich mass transfer problems with some cost function. An optical problem is specified by a function defining a particular family of supporting surfaces for the optical element. We introduce the notion of geometric equivalence between optical and transport problems, which is directly related to the possibility of formulating an optical design problem as a mass transfer problem. A necessary condition for such equivalence is derived in the semi-discrete setting. It allows a transport representation to be ruled out without choosing a cost function in advance. The condition is applied to the near-field refractor problem and to the design of two refracting surfaces transforming a spherical beam into a spherical or collimated beam. For these problems, the necessary condition is shown to fail in physically admissible configurations. We also study an optical element with a single working surface and an arbitrary regular incident wavefront. In the far field, geometric equivalence to a mass transfer problem requires a planar or spherical wavefront, whereas in the near field with a planar target, the necessary condition fails for an arbitrary smooth wavefront.
item.dc:creator: Albert A. Mingazov

item.title: Redetermination of the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients of BaMgF4
item.description: arXiv:2611.09250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: BaMgF4 (BMF) has the potential to serve as a platform material for vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) nonlinear optics owing to its ferroelectricity and high UV transparency down to 130 nm. However, the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients reported for BMF span approximately one order of magnitude, hindering a reliable assessment of its potential for nonlinear optical applications. Here, we redetermined these coefficients by combining Maker fringe, wedge, and single-pass second-harmonic-generation measurements at a fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm. Our results establish that all the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients of BMF lie in the range of 0.01-0.04 pm/V. We determined d31 to be 0.035 pm/V, which is among the largest coefficients of BMF, while it has been underestimated relative to the other coefficients in previous studies. Although d31 is not the largest coefficient, the use of its long corresponding coherence length is beneficial for quasi-phase matching, particularly for VUV generation, where the fabrication of lower-order quasi-phase-matching structures is crucial.
item.dc:creator: Shoichi Ui, Simon J. Herr, Gaetano G. M. Bonetti, Ingo Breunig, Fraunk K\"uhnemann, Matthias Bickermann, Hiroki Tanaka

item.title: TwinLight: A Multi-Timescale Physical-Layer-Aware T-API-Compliant Optical Domain Controller Digital Twin
item.description: arXiv:2611.09359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate TwinLight, an open-source optical-network digital twin acting as an optical domain controller. Its T-API REST and telemetry streaming interfaces expose a physical-layer engine that combines a GNPy steady-state baseline with four analytical transients.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Natalino, Piotr Lechowicz, Renato Ambrosone, Enrico Miotto, Vittorio Curri, Paolo Monti

item.title: Reconstructing intracell polarization with calibrated sapphire-window optics for collimated blue-light generation in a rubidium cell
item.description: arXiv:2611.09441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the polarization dependence of collimated blue light (CBL) generated near 420~nm by resonant four-wave mixing in thermal rubidium vapor in a sapphire-window cell driven at 780 and 776~nm. Sapphire windows can transform the polarization of pump light before it reaches the vapor, complicating the interpretation of polarization-dependent nonlinear emission. We measured the 780-nm pump Stokes state at an external before-cell reference plane to calibrate the common HWP/QWP preparation optics and recorded 266 off-resonant external output Stokes states after the complete sapphire-window rubidium cell at 90, 100, and 110~$^\circ$C in two propagation orientations. Direct paired-wavelength measurements show a mean before-cell 780/776 separation of $4.29^\circ$ and temperature- and orientation-specific complete-cell rotations of $22.20^\circ$--$32.02^\circ$, with rms residuals of $4.83^\circ$--$12.87^\circ$. Using this calibrated co-prepared pump description, we analyzed 2574 measurements of total spectrally filtered 420-nm CBL intensity. Across the six temperature--orientation data sets, a complete nine-coefficient second-order response yielded cross-validated $R^2$ values of 0.636 to 0.828. These paired-wavelength measurements establish, for each temperature--orientation data set, a fixed relative Stokes-space map between the two co-prepared pump trajectories, with the residual of this mapping defining the experimental uncertainty of the correlated two-pump reduction used in the response model. Thus, the resulting framework combines a reconstructed vapor-entrance polarization coordinate with direct two-wavelength calibration of the assembled cell and provides a practical basis for polarization-controlled nonlinear-optical experiments in sapphire-window vapor cells.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Ashby, David Bostanjyan, Mikayel Khanbekyan

item.title: Interface-driven second harmonic generation in indium tin oxide/gold nanolayers: density and mass discontinuities matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.09471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Second harmonic generation from transparent conductive oxides and metals is traditionally attributed to Coulomb, magnetic Lorentz, and convective sources. We show that this picture is incomplete in deeply subwavelength indium tin oxide/gold bilayers. Measurements reveal two robust spectral features, a broad maximum near 1000 nm and an epsilon-near-zero peak near 1350 nm, that persist across wide variations in material and excitation parameters. Hydrodynamic-Maxwell simulations identify an interface-specific convective mechanism activated by freeelectron density and effective-mass discontinuities at the oxide-metal boundary. As electronic homogenization develops across the bilayer, the response evolves toward one described by conventional Coulomb, Lorentz, and leading convective terms. These results establish second harmonic generation as a sensitive probe of interface-driven nonlinearities and suggest a broader role for electronic discontinuities in shaping nonlinear optical processes at surface and buried material interfaces.
item.dc:creator: J. Arya, D. Ramonell, J. Trull, N. Akozbek, M. Scalora, C. Cojocaru

item.title: A hair-thin implant opens the entire depth of the mouse brain to revisiting the same structures at subcellular resolution
item.description: arXiv:2611.09481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrathin multimode-fibre endoscopes provide minimally invasive access to subcellular structures throughout the depth of the mouse brain. Here we introduce a chronically implantable interface with a diameter of 144 {\mu}m, about the thickness of a human hair, that extends this capability to longitudinal imaging, enabling repeated access to the same fine structures over extended periods. The system supports weeks-long tracking of individual dendritic spines, allowing quantitative comparison of their dynamics and survival across dendritic compartments. We further demonstrate longitudinal intracellular calcium imaging during spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity in the same cells across days, as well as repeated measurements of blood flow in the same vessels across multiple brain regions. This chronic endomicroscopic platform provides stable, minimally invasive optical access for longitudinal subcellular-resolution imaging of brain structure, activity and blood flow across depth.
item.dc:creator: Miroslav Stib\r{u}rek, Tom\'a\v{s} Pik\'alek, Petra Ondr\'a\v{c}kov\'a, Kristina Herz\'anov\'a, Adrian Lorenz, Andr\'e Gomes, Julia Henschke, Endre Levente Marosi, Bhargavi Murthy, Petra Kolb\'abkov\'a, Hongbo Jia, Sanja Bauer Mikulovic, Janelle Pakan, Alessio Attardo, Hana Uhl\'i\v{r}ov\'a, Tom\'a\v{s} \v{C}i\v{z}m\'ar

item.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.09630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.
item.dc:creator: Ohad Silbiger, Yakir Hadad

item.title: Multipole Decomposition of Moving Sources
item.description: arXiv:2611.09654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cartesian multipole moments are widely used to analyze and engineer radiation, but the usual relations for their radiated fields assume a wavevector-independent source frequency. For moving sources, Doppler shifts make the frequency depend on the wavevector, so the radiated fields predicted from the moments generally carry errors proportional to v/c. From charge conservation in the laboratory frame, we derive a multipole decomposition of moving sources that retains the usual moments but evaluates their contributions at Doppler-shifted wavenumbers and adds a convection-current term. Requiring no rest frame, it applies to moving matter and to excitation patterns in synthetic motion through media at rest, including superluminal ones. The decomposition also extends to nonuniform translation and to nonrigid patterns with curved spectral supports. Exact calculations for moving electric, magnetic, and toroidal dipoles confirm the decomposition and attribute the different radiation of a dipole in moving matter and in synthetic motion to the laboratory moments that each kind of motion induces. For an anapole, these moments decide whether it radiates. An anapole carried by uniformly moving matter remains nonradiating, whereas an excitation pattern with the same electric and toroidal dipoles radiates in synthetic motion. The decomposition thus makes multipolar analysis available for moving matter and for excitation patterns in synthetic motion, and it opens the way to designing their radiation.
item.dc:creator: Shuhang Chen, Yutong Li, Xinmeng Wang, Qi Zhu

item.title: Magnon-polaritons in terahertz resonators based on antiferromagnets with weak ferromagnetism
item.description: arXiv:2611.09673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Terahertz magnon-polaritons in antiferromagnets with weak ferromagnetism are theoretically investigated using YFeO$_3$ as an example. Dispersion relations are obtained for the quasi-ferromagnetic and quasi-antiferromagnetic modes. It is shown that the intrinsic Fabry--Perot resonances of the magnetic slab provide strong coupling, but their low quality factor limits the cooperativity. The photonic crystal cavity increases the cooperativity of the quasi-antiferromagnetic mode from $C\sim6$ to $C\sim41$ at 300K and to $2.2\times10^3$ at 63K.
item.dc:creator: Arina A. Luzgina, Alexey A. Kraev, Shixun Cao, Anatolii K. Zvezdin, Vladimir I. Belotelov

item.title: Vertically-coupled microring resonators for lithium niobate on insulator integrated photonics
item.description: arXiv:2611.09683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and demonstrate lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) microring resonators that are verticallycoupled to index-matched silicon-rich silicon nitride (SiN x ) access waveguides as an alternative to conventional lateral coupling schemes for integrated photonics applications. The wafer-scalable fabrication process involves a planarization step exploiting a single-step and reproducible spin-coating of a SU-8 epoxy spacer layer which allows a controlled separation to be established between the resonator and its access waveguide. The resulting multimode and single-mode microring resonators exhibit, for their fundamental TE 0 mode, intrinsic quality factors of 4.0 x 10 5 and 3.4 x 10 5 , respectively.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ement Selva (LAAS-PHOTO), Sarah Umme Tabassum (LAAS-PHOTO), Kumar Kinjalk (LAAS-PHOTO), Adrian Laborde (LAAS-TEAM, LAAS-TEAM), Antoine Monmayrant (LAAS-PHOTO), Olivier Gauthier-Lafaye (LAAS-PHOTO, LAAS), St\'ephane Calvez (LAAS-PHOTO, LAAS)

item.title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
item.description: arXiv:2611.09690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous optical injection locking of an integrated pair of photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide. Due to fabrication-induced disorder, the two nanolasers exhibit distinct emission wavelengths, allowing their individual locking ranges to be resolved as a function of the injection-laser detuning and power. We identify a region where both nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the master laser. To probe this collective locked state, the two nanolasers are independently pump-modulated at distinct radio frequencies. A beat note at the difference frequency appears only within the overlap region, providing a direct RF signature of simultaneous locking. These results establish RF beating as a compact diagnostic of common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.
item.dc:creator: Jan-Niklas Topf, Roberto Gajardo, Guillaume Huyet, Fabrice Raineri, Guilhem Madiot

item.title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.09783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Infrared spectroscopy is a key tool to study complex structural dynamics in molecular systems. However, resolving weak or broad vibrational modes is challenging due to their rapid decay. Here, we demonstrate a technique to significantly extend the detectable lifetime - and thereby spectral resolution - of molecular signatures by employing synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. Utilizing a Cr:ZnS laser system and a nonlinear ZnGeP2 crystal, we achieve a 10-fold increase in the electric field strength of the infrared molecular signal, yielding a two-orders of magnitude enhancement in dynamic range and a 2-fold increase in the signal-to-noise ratio. Using isopropyl alcohol as a model system, we demonstrate that OPA-enhanced detection extends the observable window of vibrational modes up to 72 %. This approach allows for the reconstruction of high-fidelity molecular fingerprints that resolve complex vibrational relaxation pathways and weak structural dynamics, previously hidden within the background and noise, providing a pathway for new high-sensitivity and time-resolved studies of complex chemical structures.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Revuelta, Gerard Faustino, Ka Fai Mak, Ferenc Krausz, Nicholas Karpowicz

item.title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.
item.dc:creator: G. Ortenzi, G. Roberti, M. Sommacal

item.title: Disentangling Spin and Orbital Contributions in the Search for Altermagnetic Terahertz Conversion in RuO2
item.description: arXiv:2611.09098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rutile RuO2 has emerged as a prominent candidate altermagnet, yet the microscopic origin of its reported charge-angular-momentum conversion remains unsettled. Recent theoretical and experimental advances have highlighted a potentially dominant role of orbital transport, raising a fundamental ambiguity between spin- and orbital-mediated conversion in RuO2. Here, we report the first experimental disentanglement of the spin- and orbital-to-charge conversion channels in RuO2 heterostructures using terahertz emission spectroscopy. We identify Fe as a predominantly spin-current injector, whereas Ni and permalloy predominantly inject orbital currents, revealing a substantial orbital contribution to ultrafast terahertz emission. Under controlled spin-current injection, we find no evidence for inverse altermagnetic spin-splitting effect. Instead, the observed anisotropy is consistent with an anisotropic inverse spin Hall response that is strongly conditioned by the near-interface environment. Under orbital-current injection, the anisotropy is markedly weaker, indicating that orbital-to-charge conversion is largely isotropic in RuO2. Our results establish orbital transport and interface-conditioned spin Hall conversion as key to terahertz emission from RuO2, underscoring the need to disentangle spin, orbital, and interfacial contributions before assigning anisotropy to altermagnetism.
item.dc:creator: Jiahao Liu, Yuxiao Mo, Tongyang Guan, Wenhui Fang, Yongwei Cui, Wentao Qin, Zhe Yuan, Lishu Zhang, Zhensheng Tao, Yizheng Wu

item.title: Absolute Calibration of a Broadband Transmission Grating Spectrometer from 5 to 400 nm with Uncertainty Estimates
item.description: arXiv:2611.09288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the absolute calibration of a transmission grating spectrometer (TGS) with uncertainty estimates in the 5--400 nm range using synchrotron radiation at the BEAR beamline at Elettra light source in Trieste, Italy. Firstly, the spectral responsivity of a Si photodiode in the spectrometer was absolutely calibrated with respect to the absolutely-calibrated beamline photodiode. Subsequently, this photodiode was used to calibrate the transmittance of Zr and Al thin-film filters, along with bulk MgF$_2$ and UV-grade fused silica windows at their operating positions in the spectrometer to minimize mounting-induced uncertainties. Next, the quantum efficiency of the spectrometer's CCD camera was calibrated over the 5--400 nm range. Lastly, three gratings with line densities of 10000, 3000, and 1000 lines/mm were calibrated for spectroscopy in the ranges extending from soft X-ray to extreme-, vacuum- and deep-ultraviolet (DUV) wavelengths, respectively. The combination of various filters and gratings enables absolutely calibrated spectroscopy with high versatility across a broad wavelength range from soft X-rays to DUV.
item.dc:creator: E. Chebykin, A. E. H. Gaballah, R. van der Horst, A. Giglia, N. Mahne, M. van de Kerkhof, M. D. Ackermann, M. Bayraktar

item.title: Complex Hyperspin Machine and Symmetry Quenching: Benchmark and scaling up to millions of degrees of freedom
item.description: arXiv:2611.09324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driven-dissipative oscillator networks have been proposed to simulate spin models on physical hardware, mostly focusing on systems of binary (Ising) spins, or systems of spin vectors in low dimensions. The equalized hyperspin machine was recently introduced to provide a single platform to simulate general models of $N$ coupled spin vectors with tunable dimension $D$, realizing dynamical annealing protocols to vary the spin dimensionality in time. These schemes are limited to real spins coupled via real coupling matrices. We propose a generalization of the hyperspin machine that works with complex fields and deals with complex Hermitian coupling matrices, implementing an amplitude equalization scheme. This system, which we name complex hyperspin machine, can work on optimization problems with complex valued hyperspins that can be cast on complex $D$-vector Hamiltonians. We benchmark the machine against a differential evolution (DE) algorithm on complex $D=2$ hyperspins up to $N=80$, showing that the fraction of instances where a lower-energy solution is found grows with system size and coupling density, reaching $92.5\%$ at the largest considered sizes. When the DE finds a lower-energy solution, the machine still reaches a median relative energy deviation that lies between $10^{-15}$ and $10^{-12}$ while running at substantially lower computational cost. Using the complex nature of the field, we introduce a new dimensional reduction protocol that we name symmetry quenching, which collapses complex variables that map to XY spins onto real Ising spins by switching on the parametric pump. We show on Max-Cut instances with known ground states that symmetry quenching outperforms a fixed-pump Ising machine, reaching exact ground states in the presence of equalization. We scale the system to $N=10^6$ hyperspins, or $8\times10^6$ dynamical variables, on a Hermitian sparse two-dimensional lattice.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Piacenti, Marcello Calvanese Strinati, Claudio Conti

item.title: Stable, High-Charge, Laser-Driven VHEE Beams for Preclinical Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.09329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laser-driven plasma accelerators (LPAs) are promising sources of very-high-energy-electron (VHEE) beams for medical applications, but increasing charge per pulse while maintaining pointing stability remains challenging. We demonstrate laser-accelerated beams with total charge per pulse reaching (559 $\pm$ 56) pC using an 80 TW laser system. The spectra have a dominant component at 40-60 MeV and a high-energy tail extending to approximately 200 MeV. Pointing jitter measured in air at the irradiation target plane reaches as low as 0.7 mrad. The beams were used for VHEE irradiation experiments involving a 10 mm region of interest through a 40 mm depth at 400 $\pm$ 20 mGy/pulse. Spectral reproducibility is quantified over fixed-setting shot sequences. Particle-in-cell simulations produce a peak-and-tail spectrum through acceleration in successive bubbles associated with a strongly modified plasma wake, providing a plausible mechanism for maintaining substantial accelerated charge despite strong beam loading. Dose-weighted time-of-flight calculations indicate an effective pulse dose rate of $10^{12}$ Gy/s and average dose rates of tens of Gy/min. These results establish an LPA operating regime relevant to preclinical VHEE irradiation.
item.dc:creator: Chaitanya Varma, Camilla Giaccaglia, Julien Gautier, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, Pascal Rousseau, Alessandro Flacco

item.title: Inversion symmetry breaking by interlayer hybridization in a tetralayer van der Waals heterostructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.09669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inversion symmetry breaking unlocks a broad range of physical phenomena fundamental for modern technologies, motivating efforts to engineer noncentrosymmetric materials. In this context, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, which naturally lack inversion symmetry, have emerged as a versatile platform for valley physics, strong excitonic effects, and nonlinear optics. However, in their hexagonal stacking phase, inversion symmetry is restored in even-layer stacks and bulk form, suppressing these effects and limiting applications. In this work, inversion symmetry breaking is demonstrated in a vertically stacked tetralayer heterostructure assembled from two intrinsically centrosymmetric bilayer flakes, as evidenced by second harmonic generation measurements with an intensity comparable to that of their constituent monolayer. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical estimations indicate that effective symmetry breaking in the tetralayer heterostructure is driven by interlayer hybridization, giving rise to pronounced electronic and phononic signatures. This symmetry breaking further induces polar anisotropy, with an intensity ratio reaching 2.36. We propose that asymmetric contributions from excitons to the second harmonic optical dipole may influence this behavior. These findings establish interlayer coupling as a critical mechanism for introducing inversion symmetry breaking and tuning the optical response of van der Waals heterostructures, providing a powerful strategy for photonics and optoelectronics in two-dimensional materials.
item.dc:creator: Juan C. Arias-Mu\~noz, Cuiju Yu, Nianze Shang, Christopher P. Edwards, Zixuan Ning, Farzaneh Bouzari, Rodolfo Canet-Albiach, Seyed Hossein Hosseini-Shokouh, Ruihuan Fang, Hanlin Fang, Sanshui Xiao, Jose L. Lado, Zhipei Sun

item.title: Cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation from Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O
item.description: arXiv:2611.09705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O provide a solid-state setting for creating giant optical nonlinearities. Here, we use second-harmonic generation (SHG) to study Rydberg excitons in a doubly resonant optical microcavity designed to enhance both the pump and second-harmonic fields. We observe even-parity exciton states in an optical cavity and extend cavity-based measurements of Rydberg excitons up to $n=10$. The SHG intensity depends strongly on pump cavity detuning, showing the dominant role of the microcavity is the enhancement of the intra-cavity pump field. Analysis reveals an additional enhancement from the resonant second-harmonic cavity giving an overall SHG enhancement factor of $21 \pm 2$ inside the microcavity. These results establish cavity-enhanced SHG spectroscopy as a valuable tool for studying Rydberg excitons in microcavities and provide a pathway towards exploiting optical nonlinearities in Rydberg exciton polariton systems.
item.dc:creator: Horatio Q. X Wong, Krzysztof Sawicki, Madeleine Fisher, Stephen A. Lynch, Wolfgang Langbein, Sai Kiran Rajendran, Hamid Ohadi, Matthew P. A. Jones, Liam A. P. Gallagher

item.title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.
item.dc:creator: Usman Khan, Daniel Lopez, Venkat Aneesh Padmasola, Nirmal Dangi, Santosh Kumar, Yuping Huang

item.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
item.description: arXiv:2611.09752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.
item.dc:creator: Joohyung Song, James I. Kwon, Edo Waks, Saikat Guha, Chaohan Cui

item.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
item.description: arXiv:2611.09841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.
item.dc:creator: Elias R. Koch, Albert Gallem\'i, Cl\`audia L\'opez, Finn Petersen, Julien Javaloyes, Svetlana V. Gurevich

item.title: Effective skyrmion number for mixed polarization states of light
item.description: arXiv:2605.24293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polarization skyrmions are usually characterized through a unit Stokes vector field, which defines a map from the transverse plane to the Poincar\'e (Bloch) sphere and allows one to assign a skyrmion number under appropriate boundary conditions. This description assumes complete polarization. In many optical situations, however, the local polarization state is partially polarized and is therefore described by a spectral polarization matrix rather than by a single Jones vector. We formulate a density-matrix-based effective extension of the skyrmion-number construction for statistically stationary, quasi-monochromatic paraxial fields in terms of the normalized spectral polarization matrix. Its eigenvectors define two orthogonal polarization eigenstates, corresponding to antipodal points on the sphere, while the eigenvalue imbalance is fixed by the local degree of polarization (DoP) $P(\mathbf r)$. Averaging the opposite skyrmion-density contributions of these two eigenpolarizations leads to an effective skyrmion number in which the usual pure-state density is weighted by $P(\mathbf r)$. The resulting quantity reduces to the conventional skyrmion number for fully polarized fields and assigns zero weight to locally unpolarized regions. In general, it is not an integer topological invariant; rather, it is an integrated effective measure, constructed from local Stokes parameters, which can be interpreted geometrically as a DoP-weighted signed solid-angle integral of the polarization eigentexture on the Poincar\'e sphere. We illustrate the construction with a regular analytic family of polarization eigentextures with winding order $m$ and fixed radial DoP profiles, showing how the effective number depends jointly on the winding order and on the spatial overlap between the DoP and the skyrmion density.
item.dc:creator: Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero, \'Angel S. Sanz

item.title: Emergent Non-Equilibrium Emission Profiles via Luminescent Angle Restriction for Photovoltaic Energy Conversion
item.description: arXiv:2607.20783v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The detailed-balance method determines photovoltaic conversion efficiencies by relating non-equilibrium converter operation to an equilibrium reference state. Conventionally, the angular and spectral radiative channels are assumed to be defined by the equilibrium absorptivity and emissivity, with the photon chemical potential setting their occupation. The spatial distribution of emission must also be considered when radiative energy is redistributed within a complex nanophotonic converter architecture. Here we analyze this redistribution with a proposed luminescent angle restrictor, in which a flat-plate photovoltaic absorber is coupled to an overlayer with vertically aligned nanorods. The nanorod layer is nearly transparent to near-normal sunlight, while oblique photovoltaic luminescence can be absorbed, re-emitted, and partially returned to the absorber. To calculate the operating emission profile, we develop a Markov-chain transport model with an absorbing-chain formulation that enforces microscopic reversibility for local optical transitions while determining the spatially distributed steady-state emission rates. The model recovers the flat-plate detailed-balance limit and predicts voltage-dependent external emission profiles from the coupled architecture. Under idealized conditions, this non-equilibrium angular redistribution increases conversion efficiency relative to the conventional flat-plate reference. We further evaluate nanorod photoluminescence quantum yield, angular restriction, orientational disorder, and Auger recombination to identify practical constraints on the proposed architecture. These results show how detailed-balance limits for photovoltaic structures can depend on internal radiative energy redistribution and the resulting non-equilibrium emission profile, beyond what can be inferred from the macroscopic equilibrium optical response alone.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan McTague (Department of Chemistry, University of California, Irvine), Rivi Ratnaweera (Department of Chemistry, Texas A&M University), Matthew Sheldon (Department of Chemistry, University of California, Irvine, Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of California, Irvine)

item.title: Undulating Diamond Photonic Crystal in the Royal Jewel Butterfly: Circumventing Refractive Index Limits to Defy Iridescence
item.description: arXiv:2608.08540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The modest refractive-indices of biomolecules place fundamental constraints on the optical performance of natural photonic organisms. To overcome this limitation, organisms reshape basic optical structures into hierarchical architectures, exhibiting performance rivals that of high-index materials. Here we show how the Royal Jewel butterfly (Hypochrysops polycletus) employs such a strategy to circumvent the low refractive-index of chitin to achieve an unusual combination of intense structural colouration and remarkably weak angular dependence. A single-diamond photonic crystal, which was hailed as the 'holy grail' and documented only in beetles and weevils, has now been discovered in the butterfly. It deforms into a hierarchically undulated superstructure guided by basal lamina and correlated with quasi-twinning boundaries with mirror symmetry. The scale surface is thus fully terminated by inclined {111} facets essential for fundamental bandgap, producing bright specular Bragg reflection at intermediate to high angles and low-angle radiation enabled by simultaneously coupling localised resonances populated through anisotropic Bloch transport, thereby transforming an otherwise strongly angle-dependent photonic crystal into a vivid, angle-robust optical structure. Following this optical concept, an artificially angle-insensitive optical prototype was fabricated through two-photon polymerisation, validating the mechanism as a transferable design principle at the intersection of fundamental nanophotonics and bio-inspired engineering.
item.dc:creator: Yuanbo Li, Shuo Huang, Xi Wang, Congcong Cui, Hao Chen, Yuqin Xiong, Wang Zhang, Matthias Saba, Xueyan Feng, Bo Chen, Yuanyuan Cao, Lu Han

item.title: Hidden transverse-flow topology in partially coherent structured light
item.description: arXiv:2608.14923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial coherence is commonly viewed as a mechanism that reduces contrast or smooths intensity structure. Here we show that it can also encode hidden transverse-flow topology. Starting from the cross-spectral density, we formulate a generalized transverse flux, an effective velocity field, and the associated flux trajectories for quasi-monochromatic partially coherent paraxial beams. This construction converts two-point correlation phases into local transport information and reduces to the usual coherent energy-flow picture in the single-mode limit. Because the generalized flux is obtained through a local differential operation on the cross-spectral density, the proposed trajectories are, in principle, reconstructible from sufficiently resolved phase-sensitive measurements of the complex second-order coherence function, subject to the regularization required by numerical differentiation. Two analytical beam families expose this hidden topology. In twisted Gaussian Schell-model beams, a Gaussian intensity hides a distributed rotational flow with nonzero vorticity. In Laguerre-Christoffel-Darboux beams, sources with identical intensity profiles can have different flux topology, producing either spiral or purely radial trajectories. Thus, intensity and coherence magnitude do not exhaust the physical information contained in the cross-spectral density: partial coherence can reorganize the hidden topology of transverse optical transport.
item.dc:creator: Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero, \'Angel S. Sanz

item.title: Observation of pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.04827v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Photonic pseudospins enable selective excitation and routing of light, but perturbations that mix opposite pseudospins can induce backscattering in helical edge channels. Here, we experimentally demonstrate pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals, combining pseudospin selectivity with nonreciprocal unidirectional propagation. By jointly engineering lattice deformation and magnetic bias, we control dipolar-quadrupolar band inversions and construct interfaces supporting pseudospin-selective chiral channels. Microwave near-field and transmission measurements reveal a single chiral edge branch that is selectively excited by only one source handedness and exhibits pronounced nonreciprocal transport. Extending this mechanism to multidomain structures, we combine two pseudospin channels into a common waveguide, separate them into distinct outputs, and route them through intersecting interfaces. These configurations realize a nonreciprocal photonic pseudospin multiplexer and demultiplexer, together with a waveguide crossing exhibiting average measured crosstalk of -14.1 and -15.8 dB for its two input channels. Our results present an experimental route to integrating pseudospin-selective channel control with chiral edge transport, providing a foundation for nonreciprocal photonic networks that use pseudospin to organize and route multiple wave channels.
item.dc:creator: Chengle Fan, Kaizhou Shi, Xiang Xi, Zhen Gao

item.title: Analytical Markov Chain for Spatiotemporal Flux Evolution of the Inner Filter Effect in Fluorescent Media
item.description: arXiv:2607.11815v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Characterizing emission and decay time spectra in multi-component fluorescent media is essential for identifying intrinsic material properties and optimizing detectors. However, wavelength evolution from the secondary inner filter effect (IFE) distorts these observable spectra. While Monte Carlo (MC) ray-tracing can simulate this distortion, accumulating adequate tracking statistics requires long computation times, which hinders parameter optimization within high-dimensional spaces. This paper presents an analytical Markovian transport model based on spatiotemporal decoupling. A Laplace transform converts the multi-nested convolution integrals over continuous domains into a discrete Markov transition matrix, reducing the computational complexity from an exponential scale with respect to wavelength bins $N_{\lambda}$ and cascade order $n$, $\mathcal{O}(N_{\lambda}^n)$, to a linear scale, $\mathcal{O}(N_{\lambda} + n)$. The resulting algebraic solutions evaluate transient decay time spectra as a continuum superposition of Gamma wave packets and predict steady-state wavelength spectrum distortions driven by the IFE within a sub-second timescale. Validations across orthogonal and front-face spectrometer configurations show that the calculated spectra match MC simulations in lineshape. This model can serve as a fast forward engine to accelerate parameter space screening, provide early-stage detector design references, and act as a physics-constrained input for event vertex reconstruction algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Xuhui Yang, Guofu Cao
